description: Add the per-tool build/install scripts, engineering records, and README that the repo requires for every tool (modeled EXACTLY on tools/size and tools/limit), integrate muntutils into the tools build chain without breaking pcopy/pmove, then run the full validation pass and commit on the feature branch. Depends on FEAT-002 (sources must exist).
steps: Create tools/muntutils/build.sh modeled on tools/size/build.sh: `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, ROOT computed two dirs up. Search for a derived C compiler in order ($ROOT/tools/gcc/build/gcc/xgcc, .../gcc, $ROOT/tools/gcc/gcc-16.2.0/build/gcc/xgcc, .../gcc) with MEARVK_GCC override and system gcc fallback; ALSO search for a derived C++ compiler (xg++/g++ under the same build dirs) with a matching override (e.g. MEARVK_GXX) and system g++ fallback. CFLAGS `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2` for the C TU; CXXFLAGS `-std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2` for the C++ TUs. Emit MEARVK-META flags ONLY when advertised, guarded by `"$CC" --help=common 2>/dev/null | grep -q -- '-fme-metadata'`: `-fme-metadata -fme-metadata-edition=Ubuntu.Determinant.Beta.Restricted -fme-metadata-version=1.00 -fme-metadata-company=MEARVK -fme-metadata-source=tools/muntutils/<file>`; else print `warning: selected compiler does not advertise -fme-metadata; building without metadata emission` and build without them. Compile the C TU with the C compiler, the C++ TUs with the C++ compiler, then link with the C++ compiler into ./muntutils. Print `built <out> with <cc>/<cxx>`.

Create tools/muntutils/install.sh modeled on tools/size/install.sh (tiny): `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, `PREFIX="${PREFIX:-/usr/local/bin}"`, default CC/CXX (`CC="${CC:-cc}"`, `CXX="${CXX:-c++}"`), `mkdir -p "$PREFIX"`, compile the C TU and C++ TUs and link into muntutils, `install -m 0755 muntutils "$PREFIX/muntutils"`, `echo "muntutils installed to $PREFIX/muntutils"`.

Create tools/muntutils/Makefile modeled on tools/pcopy/Makefile with all/install/uninstall/clean targets so the tool slots into the tools/Makefile `$(MAKE) -C` chain. Use CC=gcc, CXX=g++, CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS as above but WITHOUT -Werror in the Makefile only if needed for portability (prefer keeping -Wall -Wextra -O2; match pcopy which uses -Wall -Wextra -O2). Build the C and C++ objects and link into muntutils. install target installs the muntutils binary to $(DESTDIR)$(BINDIR)/muntutils.

Integrate into tools/Makefile: change `TOOLS := pcopy pmove` to `TOOLS := pcopy pmove muntutils`, add a `muntutils:` target that runs `$(MAKE) -C muntutils all`, add it to install/uninstall/clean, and add it to .PHONY. Keep pcopy/pmove exactly as they are (pmove still depends on pcopy). CRITICAL: muntutils is independent of pcopy/pmove, so the `muntutils:` target MUST NOT depend on pcopy or pmove (no prerequisite edge). This is important because tools/pcopy/pcopy.c has a PRE-EXISTING, out-of-scope build bug (line 62 `#define PCOPY_IOCTL_MAGIC 0xPC`, an invalid C literal rejected by GCC 11.5.0) that breaks the aggregate `all` target; you MUST NOT fix or modify pcopy/pmove (out of scope, unauthorized). Ordering muntutils with no dependency edge lets `make -C tools muntutils` build muntutils successfully even while `make -C tools all` fails on the pre-existing pcopy bug.

Create tools/muntutils/README.md modeled on tools/size/README.md and tools/limit/README.md voice: sections for Build with the derived GCC (candidate search + MEARVK_GCC/MEARVK_GXX override + -fme-metadata block for version 1.00 + system fallback note), Build directly (cc/g++ one-liners), Behavior (describe both capabilities), Safe-by-default statement (default writes slim tree to a separate out dir, never overwrites; --in-place/--apply opt-in creates a .bak backup first), Reachability limits caveat (static analysis cannot fully resolve dynamic dispatch, function pointers, dlopen/dlsym, reflection, preprocessor conditionals; the tool is conservative and keeps uncertain functions and reports what it could not resolve), Report audience note (plain-language summary for an ordinary adult user plus detailed numbers for a programmer), Engineering records list, Scope, Versioning (initial 1.00). Include the metadata 'not a legal ownership/fiduciary/authorization claim' note like size/limit. Include the NCSU attribution line EXACTLY: 'Program based on Science at NCSU - Max Rupplin - MEARVK LLC 2026.' No em dashes in prose.

Create tools/muntutils/muntutils.hss (HSS Specification) modeled on tools/size/size.hss: Identity (Tool muntutils, Language C11 + C++17, Purpose, Current tool version 1.00, Metadata schema target MEARVK-META schema 1, Repository mearvk/Ubuntu.Determinant.Beta.Restricted), Structure, Platform behavior, Metadata, Safety (safe-by-default trimming + opt-in in-place with backup), Build Contract. Include NCSU attribution.

Create tools/muntutils/muntutils.hsss (HSSS Source/Structure Record) modeled on tools/size/size.hsss with sections: `## 1. Source`, `## 2. Specification`, `## 3. System Boundary`, `## 4. Compiler Relationship`, `## 5. Authority`, `## 6. Verification`. Document the C/C++ split, safe-by-default vs opt-in in-place, and reachability limits. Include NCSU attribution.

Create tools/muntutils/1-2-3-4.mmd modeled on tools/size/1-2-3-4.mmd with sections: title heading, `## 1 — Identity`, `## 2 — Structure`, `## 3 — Process` (numbered steps: analyze reachability -> emit slim tree to separate out dir -> measure raw/slim/compiled -> generate dual-audience report -> in-place only with explicit flag + backup), `## 4 — Evidence / Authority` (reachability is a static estimate; NCSU/MEARVK attribution is provenance, not authority), `## Change Record` (dated entry for initial 1.00 creation).

Run the full validation pass: (a) `cd tools/muntutils && ./build.sh` and confirm it builds the C+C++ program with the system gcc/g++ fallback and prints the no -fme-metadata warning; (b) `make -C tools muntutils` and confirm muntutils builds via the tools/Makefile chain (do NOT rely on `make -C tools all`, which fails on the pre-existing unrelated pcopy.c bug that is out of scope); (c) `make -C tools clean`; (d) re-run the capability 1 and capability 2 runtime checks from FEAT-002's verification against a fresh sample tree to confirm safe-by-default (originals byte-identical, slim tree in a separate out dir, in-place only with a .bak backup) and the dual-audience report.

Stage ONLY the intended files (tools/muntutils/* and the tools/Makefile edit and the .agents task files) and commit on the feature branch with a clear message. Do NOT push or open a PR (the orchestrator publishes). Leave a clean working tree.
acceptance_criteria: tools/muntutils/ contains build.sh, install.sh, Makefile, README.md, muntutils.hss, muntutils.hsss, and 1-2-3-4.mmd, all modeled on the size/limit conventions and all carrying the exact NCSU attribution line.

tools/Makefile has a muntutils target (with no dependency on pcopy/pmove) and `make -C tools muntutils` builds muntutils successfully despite the pre-existing unrelated pcopy.c bug; `make -C tools clean` cleans muntutils too; pcopy/pmove targets left unchanged.
tools/muntutils/build.sh builds the C+C++ program with the system gcc/g++ fallback and prints the standard no -fme-metadata warning in this sandbox.
README documents both capabilities, the safe-by-default trimming behavior, the --in-place/--apply opt-in with backup, the reachability limitations, the dual-audience report, and version 1.00.
The engineering records (.hss, .hsss, 1-2-3-4.mmd) follow the exact section structure of the size/limit templates.
Work is committed on branch feat/muntutils-source-trimmer-sizer with a clean tree; nothing pushed.
verification: Run `cd tools/muntutils && ./build.sh`; confirm exit code 0 and the no -fme-metadata warning printed.
Run `make -C tools muntutils`; confirm muntutils builds (aggregate `all` is expected to fail on the pre-existing unrelated pcopy.c bug and that is acceptable); then `make -C tools clean`.
Re-run the capability-1 safe-by-default check (originals byte-identical, slim tree in separate out dir), the in-place --bak check, and the capability-2 report check.
Run `git status` to confirm a clean tree after commit and `git log --oneline -1` to confirm the commit exists on the feature branch.
findings: Implemented all deliverables in tools/muntutils/: build.sh (dual derived-compiler search MEARVK_GCC/MEARVK_GXX with system gcc/g++ fallback, per-TU -fme-metadata guarded block, C TU with gcc + C++ TUs with g++, link with g++, version 1.00), install.sh (PREFIX-based, CC/CXX defaults cc/c++), Makefile (CC=gcc CXX=g++, -Wall -Wextra -O2, builds muntutils_fs.o + muntutils_trim.o + main.o, links with CXX, all/install/uninstall/clean), README.md, muntutils.hss, muntutils.hsss, 1-2-3-4.mmd. tools/Makefile: TOOLS now 'pcopy pmove muntutils'; added a dependency-free muntutils target plus install/uninstall/clean/.PHONY entries; pcopy/pmove left unchanged (pmove still depends on pcopy). Kept the muntutils target with NO prerequisite so `make -C tools muntutils` builds even though the aggregate `all` target still fails on the PRE-EXISTING out-of-scope pcopy.c bug (line 62 `#define PCOPY_IOCTL_MAGIC 0xPC`). Did not modify pcopy/pmove or the 5 existing muntutils sources. VALIDATION all green: (a) ./build.sh exit 0 and printed exactly 'warning: selected compiler does not advertise -fme-metadata; building without metadata emission' then 'built .../muntutils with gcc/g++'; (b) `make -C tools muntutils` compiled and linked cleanly from scratch after `make -C tools clean`; (c) clean works and removes muntutils objects+binary; (d) runtime checks on a fresh sample tree: default `trim <src> --out <dir>` left originals byte-identical (sha256sum -c OK) and wrote a slim tree that correctly stubbed the dead static function `dead_helper` while keeping used/extern-linkable functions; `--in-place` created a `.bak` backup per rewritten file before rewriting; `report --slim <dir> --out <file>` produced markdown with raw stats, slim stats, compiled-artifact (.o) stats, a plain-language 'Summary for everyone', and a 'Details for a programmer' section. NOTE (out-of-scope observation, not fixed): the FEAT-002 trim engine replaces a removed body with a stub comment, so for very small dead functions the slim source-text can be slightly larger than raw; the report clamps the shrink percentage to 0.0 in that case and this did not affect any FEAT-003 acceptance criterion. Ran validation inside tools/muntutils/.validate and deleted it afterward; earlier a /tmp sample tree vanished between two separate shell sessions (sandbox /tmp cleanup across sessions, unrelated to muntutils which is strictly read-then-write and never deletes).
